cards.text: Jeremiah is the LORD's prophet, and the LORD has warned Judah that disaster is coming from the north (Jeremiah 1:5; 4:5-6). Now the LORD gives an order: go up and down the streets of Jerusalem and search her squares. He's looking for anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth.

cards.question: If the search through Jerusalem turns up someone who acts justly and seeks the truth, what will the LORD do?
The LORD would forgive Jerusalem if the search found just ___ person who acts justly.

cards.text: These people say, "As surely as the LORD lives," and it sounds so holy. But hold on.

cards.question: When the people in Jerusalem say "As surely as the LORD lives," they mean it.

cards.text: They're swearing falsely, like the dead batteries I shared that drawer with. Every one of them SWORE it still had a little charge left.
Then Jeremiah turns to the LORD: "O LORD, do not Your eyes look for truth?" The LORD struck the people, but they felt no pain.

cards.question: The LORD disciplined His people in Jerusalem, but they refused to ___.

cards.text: They've made their faces harder than stone. Friend, that's a whole city hitting snooze on the alarm, over and over and OVER.
Then Jeremiah thinks it through. Maybe these are just the poor, and they don't know the way of the LORD.

cards.question: Jeremiah is sure somebody in Jerusalem knows the way of the LORD. Who does he go to next?
Jeremiah finds that the powerful in Jerusalem keep the way of the LORD.
Jeremiah says the powerful "had broken the yoke and torn off the chains." What's that picture saying?

answers.text: They threw off the LORD's way

cards.text: So much for going to the manager. Then comes the warning: a lion from the forest, a wolf from the desert, and a leopard lying in wait near their cities.

cards.question: Why will the lion, the wolf and the leopard come against the people?

cards.text: Now the LORD asks, "Why should I forgive you?" His people have forsaken Him.

cards.question: The LORD's people have forsaken Him. What have they sworn by instead?
The LORD satisfied His people's needs, and they stayed faithful in their marriages.

cards.text: Instead the LORD calls them well-fed stallions, each one after his neighbor's wife. Then He asks, "Should I not punish them for these things?"

cards.question: Think back to the search through Jerusalem's streets. The LORD's questions show it found someone who acts justly.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives another order about the nation's vineyards: go up through them and ravage them.

cards.question: The LORD says to ravage the vineyards. But what limit does He set?
The LORD says to strip off the vineyard's branches, because they do not belong to the ___.
The LORD says only the house of Judah has been unfaithful to Him.

cards.text: And they've lied about the LORD. Not about the weather. Not about the traffic. About the LORD.

cards.question: What do the people say about the LORD?

cards.text: They say no harm will come to them, no sword, no famine. That's the group chat when somebody posts a storm warning and everybody replies, "Relax, it'll miss us."

cards.question: The people believe the prophets carry the LORD's word.

cards.text: They call the prophets wind. So the LORD God of Hosts responds.

cards.question: The people called the prophets wind. What does the LORD say He will make His words?

cards.text: And this people will be "the wood it consumes." Friend, I've worked ovens my whole life, and fire versus wood is NOT a close contest.
Then the LORD says He's bringing a distant nation against the house of Israel. An established nation, an ancient one.

cards.question: What else does the LORD say about this distant nation?

answers.text: It is coming to help them

cards.text: Their quivers are like open graves, and they're all mighty men. They'll devour the harvest and the food, the flocks and the herds, the vines and the fig trees, even sons and daughters.

cards.question: The fortified cities the people trust in will hold off this nation.

cards.text: Heavy stuff, friend. Then the LORD says, "Yet even in those days," and I'm leaning in.

cards.question: Even in those days, the LORD says He will not ___ His people completely.

cards.text: One day the people will ask, "For what offense has the LORD our God done all these things to us?" And the LORD has an answer ready.

cards.question: They served foreign ___ in their own land, so they will serve ___ in a land that is not their own.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the search is for "anyone who acts justly," and card 2's question asks what happens if the search "turns up someone who acts justly." Both come before card 3, so the baker already knows the answer to "just ___ person" is one. Card 3 also asks the same v1 fact a second time.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 10 says "Jeremiah thinks it through," but the text says "Then I said" (Jer 5:4). The text calls it speaking, not thinking.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: No story card sets up who has been unfaithful. The house of Israel hasn't been mentioned before this card. The baker can only get the answer from the test-taking cue "only," not by reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The house of Israel shows up for the first time here, next to the house of Judah, and nothing says who it is. It comes up again on card 12 ("against the house of Israel") after a whole stop about Jerusalem, so the baker may not know who is meant.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke "fire versus wood is NOT a close contest" makes light of the people being consumed, which is the judgment the line is about. The humor lands on their destruction instead of treating their situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: "I've worked ovens my whole life" doesn't fit his backstory. He was a stamper on the Millers' counter and then spent years in a junk drawer before the Dorinverse bakery. The line adds something new to his world that his story doesn't support.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 12 just said the LORD is bringing this nation "against the house of Israel." That rules out the wrong answer "It is coming to help them," and next to the setup it reads as silly.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "rescue" makes the line "He will not rescue His people completely," which a baker could argue fits the passage, since the people end up serving foreigners in a land not their own (Jer 5:19). Card 16's setup ("Yet even in those days... I'm leaning in") also points to mercy, so the two wrong answers don't sit evenly with the right one.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
